input.reasoning:
Sized backlog by story points (total 81 pts) and translated to engineering-hours using a baseline of ~7 hours/point for full-stack feature work (covering backend+frontend+QA+devops effort combined across a task), then split hours per task across roles based on task nature (e.g., CI/DevOps task weighted to DevOps, UI-heavy tasks weighted to Frontend, integration/RBAC/migration weighted to Backend, all tasks carry QA hours, DevOps also gets pipeline/deployment support on migration and payment webhooks). Applied role FTE capacity as a sanity check against a ~6-week (240 hour/FTE) delivery window: Backend capacity ~360h, Frontend ~240h, QA ~144h, DevOps ~96h. Allocated hours were kept within roughly 1.1-1.3x of nominal capacity to reflect a realistic single-sprint-cycle push (implying some schedule slip or overtime, called out as an assumption) rather than compressing scope artificially.

Per-task effort estimate (total hours, then role split):
- PW-1 CI pipeline (5 pts, High): 40h total -> DevOps 28, Backend 6, QA 6
- PW-2 Design system (8 pts, Medium): 64h -> Frontend 48, QA 8, Backend 8
- PW-3 Registration/login (8 pts, Urgent): 64h -> Backend 32, Frontend 20, QA 12
- PW-4 RBAC (13 pts, High): 104h -> Backend 56, Frontend 28, QA 20
- PW-5 Dashboard (8 pts, High): 64h -> Frontend 36, Backend 18, QA 10
- PW-6 Invoice list/detail (5 pts, Medium): 40h -> Frontend 22, Backend 12, QA 6
- PW-7 Payment integration (13 pts, Urgent): 104h -> Backend 56, QA 20, DevOps 16, Frontend 12
- PW-8 Legacy data migration (21 pts, High): 168h -> Backend 110, DevOps 30, QA 28

Role totals:
Backend: 6+8+32+56+18+12+56+110 = 298h
Frontend: 48+20+28+36+22+12 = 166h
QA: 6+8+12+20+10+6+20+28 = 110h
DevOps: 28+16+30 = 74h

These totals are within capacity envelopes (Backend 1.5 FTE ~ 360h/6wk, Frontend 1.0 FTE ~240h, QA 0.6 FTE ~144h, DevOps 0.4 FTE ~96h), giving headroom for meetings, code review, and unplanned work, though QA and DevOps are proportionally the tightest given their fractional staffing — flagged as an assumption/risk.

Non-labour costs assumed for a project of this shape: staging cloud infra, Stripe fees/test sandbox, migration tooling/data validation, and standard PM/contingency overhead not covered by the four staffed roles (project coordination is assumed absorbed by leads, so no separate PM line-item is included, but contingency is added as a line to cover schedule/estimation risk).

Priority breakdown computed by summing labour cost of tasks per priority using each task's blended role cost.

Reductions and scenarios reflect realistic descoping/deferral options, especially around the large legacy migration task (PW-8) and the medium-priority design system/invoice view work, which are the most deferable items without harming the urgent payment/auth path.

nonLabourLines.description: Staging/cloud infrastructure (CI runners, staging environment hosting) for pipeline build-out
Stripe integration sandbox, webhook testing tools, and PCI-related compliance review
Legacy Oracle data migration tooling, ETL scripts, and validation/reconciliation support
Contingency / estimation risk buffer (~10% of labour cost)

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available for this project yet; estimate is based purely on story-point sizing and role-effort judgement, not past velocity.

Story points were converted to engineering hours using a rough baseline of ~7-8 hours per point for full-stack delivery (design, build, test, review) split proportionally across roles based on task type.

A single delivery cycle of roughly 6 weeks was assumed as the sizing horizon; allocated hours run slightly above nominal FTE capacity for QA and DevOps, implying either mild overtime, schedule extension, or the need for temporary contractor support to fully absorb the backlog as scoped.

QA Engineer (0.6 FTE) and DevOps Engineer (0.4 FTE) are thinly staffed relative to backlog demand — every task requires some QA time and several require DevOps time, so these roles are the most likely schedule bottleneck.
No dedicated Project Manager role is staffed; coordination overhead is assumed to be absorbed informally by the Backend/Frontend leads and is not separately costed.

Legacy data migration (PW-8) is assumed to require significant Backend engineering effort for ETL/reconciliation logic rather than being purely a DevOps or data-team task, since no separate data engineering role is staffed.
Non-labour costs are rough placeholders for infrastructure, third-party tooling (Stripe sandbox/compliance), and migration tooling; actual vendor quotes were not available.
A 10% contingency buffer on labour cost is included to cover estimation uncertainty, given the lack of historical actuals.

reductions.description: Defer PW-8 Legacy data migration to a follow-on phase; ship the portal first with manual/CSV import fallback for legacy records.
reductions.effect: Removes ~168 hours (110 Backend, 30 DevOps, 28 QA) from this phase, cutting the single largest cost driver and easing pressure on the thinly-staffed DevOps/QA roles.

reductions.description: Descope PW-2 Design system to a minimal component set (buttons, forms, tables only; defer full theming tokens and dialogs) since it is Medium priority.
reductions.effect: Reduces Frontend hours on PW-2 from 48 to ~20, deferring theming/dialog polish to a later iteration.

reductions.description: Reduce QA hours on lower-risk UI tasks (PW-5 Dashboard, PW-6 Invoice list) by relying more on developer self-testing and automated test coverage instead of dedicated manual QA passes.
reductions.effect: Cuts QA hours on PW-5 and PW-6 by roughly half (from 16 combined to 8), acceptable given these are read-only, lower-risk views.

reductions.description: Defer the contingency buffer reduction by tightening non-labour spend: negotiate a lower-cost Stripe test/compliance setup and reuse existing cloud credits for staging infrastructure.
reductions.effect: Reduces non-labour line items (Stripe/compliance and staging infra) by roughly half, assuming existing tooling/cloud credit can be leveraged.

scenarios.name: Optimistic (full descope of migration + design system trim applied)
Pessimistic (schedule slip, QA/DevOps bottleneck requires contractor support, +20%)
